concerns.description: One logical committed-state owner across physical replicas
concerns.rationale: Physical replicas implement one logical history; ApplyCommitted alone owns the application projection, without proving the external certificate sound.
Discrete admission and provenance fit typed inputs/outputs; RecordVerification is the sole logical owner.
State/action exploration belongs to TLA+; a ConceptIR graph cannot establish temporal safety or liveness.
Multiple execution attempts realize one request; they do not create competing semantic owners.
Region/host allocation is deployment evidence; the bounded model contains no topology.

realization.strategy: Export digest-bound verification request; admit matching analyzer report.
realization.placement: Protocol replicas may span failure domains; TLC workers run on analysis hosts.
limitations: Bounded single-slot write-once voting model; no leader election, crash recovery, log replication, or liveness proof.

artifacts.claim: TLC checks three named safety invariants only for the finite supplied configuration.
Three voters, two values, one slot; no fairness assumption.
Pins tool and input digests, bounded state counts and checks.

sources.title: TLA+ language and tools
sources.supports: State/action/temporal semantics and finite model checking are separate from architecture.
